svg.title: Encrypted personal sync — the relay stores ciphertext it cannot read

g.text: Encrypted personal sync — the relay stores ciphertext it cannot read
Devices encrypt with a vault key held in their OS keychain. S3 holds immutable content-addressed objects; DynamoDB holds the revision head as a compare-and-swap.
▶ NOW
1 · Device A commits locally, then asks to push: parent sequence number plus the hashes of its encrypted objects.
2 · The Sync API checks the device's JWT and its grant on this vault.
3 · It reads the vault head and returns presigned PUT URLs only for objects the bucket does not have yet.
4 · Device A uploads ciphertext objects and the encrypted manifest with If-None-Match: immutable and deduplicated.
5 · Commit is a conditional update: head = parent + 1 only if head is still the parent. Nobody silently wins.
6 · If another device moved the head first, the push gets 409: Device A fetches, merges locally and retries.
7 · The head change flows through DynamoDB Streams to the notifier.
8 · The notifier posts 'head advanced' (ids only, no content) to the vault's other device connections.
9 · Device B is woken up over its WebSocket.
10 · Device B fetches the manifest and objects by presigned GET, checks every hash and decrypts with the vault key.
11 · It reconciles locally: fast-forward, three-way merge, or a named conflict copy; then reindexes. No silent data loss.
12 · At rest, S3 and DynamoDB add SSE-KMS with the tenant key: a second layer, not the confidentiality guarantee.
13 · Point-in-time recovery, AWS Backup plans and S3 versioning make the replica restorable.

How it flows
Device A commits locally, then asks to push: parent
sequence number plus the hashes of its encrypted objects.
The Sync API checks the device's JWT and its grant on this
vault.
It reads the vault head and returns presigned PUT URLs
only for objects the bucket does not have yet.
Device A uploads ciphertext objects and the encrypted
manifest with If-None-Match: immutable and deduplicated.
Commit is a conditional update: head = parent + 1 only if
head is still the parent. Nobody silently wins.
If another device moved the head first, the push gets 409:
Device A fetches, merges locally and retries.
The head change flows through DynamoDB Streams to the
notifier.
The notifier posts 'head advanced' (ids only, no content)
to the vault's other device connections.
Device B is woken up over its WebSocket.
Device B fetches the manifest and objects by presigned
GET, checks every hash and decrypts with the vault key.
It reconciles locally: fast-forward, three-way merge, or a
named conflict copy; then reindexes. No silent data loss.
At rest, S3 and DynamoDB add SSE-KMS with the tenant key:
a second layer, not the confidentiality guarantee.
Point-in-time recovery, AWS Backup plans and S3 versioning
make the replica restorable.
